TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_face
TABLE.COMMENT: Enrolled face embeddings. One active row per user; superseded rows are kept for audit until purged.

FIELD.NAME: embedding
FIELD.COMMENT: base64 float32 vector as returned by the face service

FIELD.NAME: dimensions
FIELD.COMMENT: Vector length; a mismatch means the model changed and the learner must re-enrol

FIELD.NAME: modelpack
FIELD.COMMENT: Which model produced this embedding

FIELD.NAME: challenge
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON record of the active-liveness challenge that gated this enrolment

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_check
TABLE.COMMENT: Result of every presence or identity check.

FIELD.NAME: contextid
FIELD.COMMENT: Where the check happened — quiz attempt context, course module context

FIELD.NAME: attemptid
FIELD.COMMENT: quiz_attempts.id when the check belongs to an exam

FIELD.NAME: sessionid
FIELD.COMMENT: Which sitting this belongs to

FIELD.NAME: kind
FIELD.COMMENT: presence | identity | enrolment

FIELD.NAME: decision
FIELD.COMMENT: pass | review | fail | fail_liveness | absent

FIELD.NAME: threshold
FIELD.COMMENT: The threshold in force at the time — do not resolve this from config when reading back

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_evidence
TABLE.COMMENT: Pointer rows for snapshots and clips; the bytes live in the Moodle file API.

FIELD.NAME: sessionid
FIELD.COMMENT: Which sitting this belongs to

FIELD.NAME: kind
FIELD.COMMENT: snapshot | clip

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: scheduled | random_sample | violation_<type>

FIELD.NAME: itemid
FIELD.COMMENT: File API itemid

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_monitored
TABLE.COMMENT: Which course modules are watched. Kept here rather than as a setting on the activity: the activities being watched belong to other plugins, and reaching into a third-party module's settings form is how you end up maintaining a fork.

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_session
TABLE.COMMENT: One sitting under monitoring, with the policy that was in force recorded on it. Without this, checks and evidence accumulate against a context with no way to say which sitting they belong to.

FIELD.NAME: attemptid
FIELD.COMMENT: quiz_attempts.id when this sitting is an exam attempt

FIELD.NAME: policy
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON snapshot of the rules enforced at the moment the sitting began, read from configuration server-side

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: active | completed | terminated | abandoned

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: what ended it, when it was not a normal finish

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Last sign of life; the cleanup task uses it to spot sittings nobody ended

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_draw
TABLE.COMMENT: Which paper a learner was given, and the seed that produced it. The seed is a pure function of learner, quiz and attempt number, so it cannot have been chosen after the fact.

FIELD.NAME: blueprint
FIELD.COMMENT: What each slot was allowed to draw from

FIELD.NAME: questionids
FIELD.COMMENT: The paper actually given, in slot order. The durable evidence: a bank edit or a core upgrade can stop the seed reproducing it, but this stays true.

TABLE.NAME: local_kaiproctor_convo
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per conversation with the assistant. An index beside the file, not instead of it: listing somebody's conversations and totalling what they use must work without opening every file they own. The transcript itself is Markdown in the user context file area, which is what deleting a user actually deletes.

FIELD.NAME: title
FIELD.COMMENT: Taken from the first question. A list of conversations all called the same thing is a list nobody can navigate.

FIELD.NAME: bytes
FIELD.COMMENT: Size of the transcript, summed per user to enforce the quota without stat-ing every file.

FIELD.NAME: remoteid
FIELD.COMMENT: The far side's id for this conversation, when the assistant keeps its own state (the Indorama service does). Without it every question through this site starts the remote conversation over, and the far side's memory of earlier turns goes unused. Null for the built-in assistant, which keeps no remote state.
